title: OAI 142 deterministic polynomial factorisation over 𝔽_p (claimed) for deterministic ES search mod p
connection: OAI 142 claims deterministic polynomial-time factoring of polynomials over prime fields; deterministic square roots mod p appear in Type I (p² ≡ −4c²d mod f).
why: Derandomising the local steps of ES search; minor but concrete.
first_step: Identify randomised steps in the repo's ES search code (square roots mod primes) and note whether deterministic alternatives matter.

title: Factoring with hints: ES as 'find a factor of 4Cp+1 in a residue class' (Coppersmith known-MSB/LSB attacks)
connection: Coppersmith factors N given half the bits of a factor; ES wants a factor of N_C = 4Cp+1 ≡ −1 mod 4C — i.e. the low bits (mod 4C) of the factor are known.
why: Known-LSB factoring (factors in a prescribed class mod M with M ≥ N^{1/4}) is polynomial time via lattices; ES's modulus 4C is tiny relative to N^{1/4}, but summing over C gives many tries.
first_step: Quantify: for which C is 4C ≥ (4Cp+1)^{1/4}? (C ≥ p^{1/3}) — then Coppersmith decides existence of a factor ≡ −1 mod 4C exactly; check whether the large-C range alone has certificates often (data).

title: Problem 298: positive density versus all-prime coverage
connection: Problem 298 ↔ ES F01, F05, F12, with feature flip F01: density existence does not imply universal existence.
why: This is a concrete example of a powerful density theorem that leaves individual inputs unresolved, useful for identifying the exact missing uniformity in ES.
first_step: Locate the density hypothesis in Bloom’s proof and ask what additional uniform lower bound on the ES candidate set would upgrade it to each prime p.
alt_first_steps: [signature-0208] Check whether the proof’s density hypothesis can be instantiated with the set of ES parameters admitting a specified denominator pattern; identify the exact density-loss step.

title: Minimal pair: Artin conjecture (conditional) vs existence of a primitive root (proved)
connection: Artin conjecture (conditional) vs existence of a primitive root (proved): they differ essentially in one feature — fixed base a vs free choice of base. ES's position: ES has free choice of certificate parameters (like free base), which suggests existence should be easier than an Artin-type fixed-witness statement.
why: Minimal pairs isolate the feature responsible for crossing the dividing line; each is a precise question about ES.
first_step: Quantify how much freedom ES has: number of 'independent' parameters vs constraint count.

title: Composite failures for 'none of x, y, z divisible by 4': exactly multiples of 16
connection: Among n ≤ 3000 the n with no ES solution having 4 ∤ x, 4 ∤ y, 4 ∤ z are 16, 32, 48, …; the analogous condition for 8 fails exactly at multiples of 32, for 9 at multiples of 9, for 5 at multiples of 5.
why: Clean local lemmas (p-adic valuation of n forces valuations of denominators); sanity checks for the variant engine.
first_step: Prove: v₂(n) ≥ 4 ⇒ 4 | some denominator; v₃(n) ≥ 2 ⇒ 9 | some denominator.

title: Sun-style refinements as data: four-square-like refinements of ES
connection: Sun formulated many 'refined Lagrange' conjectures by computer search; several were proved. Generate ES refinements automatically (x + y or z constrained to be a square, a prime, ≡ r mod m, etc.), test them to 10⁷, and keep those that never fail — new conjectures whose extra structure may make them provable or reveal hidden symmetries.
why: Automated conjecture generation found provable statements for sums of squares; ES has never been mined this way systematically (check repo).
first_step: Write a search over ~200 refinement predicates P(x, y, z, p) and test on all p ≤ 10⁶; report survivors.
refs: arXiv:2003.02592 (Machiavelo-Tsopanidis, Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations)

title: Complex multiplication specializations
connection: Look for special quadratic parameters where norm or theta expressions simplify through extra algebraic symmetry.
why: Special values might yield isolated constructive families rather than uniform coverage.
first_step: Choose a small discriminant, compute the associated norm expressions, and test whether the ES congruences simplify.

title: Sylvester waves of the restricted partition function p_{u,B}(n) evaluated at n = p
connection: Sylvester decomposed restricted partition functions into waves (polynomial part + periodic parts from roots of unity of order dividing u, B) ↔ the (★) condition is that the periodic waves of order u and B both take their extreme values at p.
why: Wave decomposition writes the condition as a sum of root-of-unity terms — a Fourier expansion over e^{2πi k/u}, e^{2πi l/B} — possibly summable over (u,B) to an exponential-sum expression for R(p).
first_step: Write the Sylvester wave for two parts explicitly (via Rademacher/Dedekind–Fourier sums) and derive R(p) as a double sum over (u,B) of root-of-unity sums; check numerically for small p.

title: Use Markoff K3 obstructions to audit local tests
connection: The Hasse-failing Markoff-type K3 family in arXiv:2504.10992 shares ES F06/F07/F13 and demonstrates why checking all local conditions need not supply a global integral point.
why: It is a concrete test case against overinterpreting ES's known local solubility.
first_step: Read the local-solubility verification in the paper and list which parts depend on the Markoff form, then test their analogues on ES modulo small prime powers.

title: U(p) vs τ(p−1) and σ(p−1)/(p−1): ρ ≈ −0.53
connection: More divisors of p−1 ⇒ fewer ES solutions (ρ(τ(p−1)) = −0.53, ρ(σ(p−1)/(p−1)) = −0.53, ρ(φ(p−1)/(p−1)) = +0.42).
why: Smooth p−1 means p ≡ 1 modulo many small numbers — the Mordell-class obstruction; links ES hardness to the Erdős–Pomerance world of smooth shifted primes.
first_step: Test whether τ(p−1) remains significant after controlling for L(1,χ_p) (partial correlation).

title: Partitions of the reciprocal mass
connection: Connect ES to restricted partition problems after multiplying by a common denominator L: 4L/p=L/x+L/y+L/z.
why: The summands are divisors of L, so this is an exact three-part divisor partition when p divides L.
first_step: For several small multiples L of p, enumerate three-divisor partitions of 4L/p.

title: OAI 182 power savings for polynomial differences at primes (claimed)
connection: OAI 182 claims power-saving Sárközy-type bounds for differences P(p), p prime; ES certificate polynomials evaluated at primes are a polynomial-at-primes family.
why: Weak link; records that difference-set methods at prime arguments now have power savings.
first_step: Check whether any ES certificate condition is a 'difference set avoids P(primes)' statement; likely close.

title: Near-isosceles solutions: smallest y − x (or z − y) at p ≡ 1 (4)
connection: Since x = y is impossible at p ≡ 1 (4), the minimal gap y − x over solutions is a fingerprint of how close the hard class comes to the degenerate locus.
why: If the minimal gap is always small (bounded or ≪ log p), near-degenerate families might give uniform certificates.
first_step: Add min(y − x) and min(z − y) to the count program; tabulate at p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 2·10⁵.
